conviction_note: Abs move 13% (option-implied event move 13.11%, own median 9.84%, Q4 guide and a 2027 update likely), p_up 55: the company reaffirmed Q3/FY/2027 in a primary document on 2026-09-10 and hyperscaler/GPU-pricing proxies since then point to strong demand, while the 33.5% 20-day fall came with a sector credit scare (CoreWeave debt) and no company news; leaning against an 8.3-pt put skew is kept small because the main counter-risk (capex/FCF and memory-cost inflation hitting the 2027 outlook) is a real line the stock can trade on. Findings sum +1.35 and the scaled number +1.3 agree by coincidence, not fitting.
bar: Company Q3 2026 guide: revenue $304-307m (+32-34% y/y), non-GAAP EPS $0.28-0.30 (https://app.sentisense.ai/stories/digitalocean-delivers-29-percent-revenue-growth-and-raises-outlook-08052026 ; https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/digitalocean-nysedocn-releases-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-04/). Street consensus is disputed: Benzinga revenue $306.8m / EPS $0.28 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DOCN/earnings-forecasts) vs Chartmill revenue $312.79m / EPS $0.33 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/DOCN/estimates). Sized against the company guide; the whisper may sit above the top end. FY26 revenue guide $1.170-1.180bn; management says growth reaches 35%+ by Q4 2026 and >50% in 2027.
positioning_check: Short interest 8.7m shares, 7.4% of float, 2.4 days to cover, falling 25% m/m, as of 2026-08-19 per equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/DOCN) -- single aggregator, no October figure found; not crowded. Baseline: 25d skew +8.34 vol pts (downside paid), put/call OI 0.62, ATM IV 164.7%, event-implied move 13.11%, run-up 5d -8.33%, 20d -33.51%, -49.7% from 52w high. MarketBeat consensus Moderate Buy (1 SB / 13 Buy / 3 Hold), avg PT ~$154.69 vs spot $91.24.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-10, 71 days into Q3 and three weeks before quarter end, CFO Matt Steinfort said in the company's own release that DigitalOcean 'remains highly confident' in its Q3 guide ($304-307m) and full-year 2026 guide ($1.170-1.180bn) and in its 2027 outlook (>50% growth); since then the stock has fallen from ~$128 (Oct 13) to $91.24 with no company news, so the price now implies doubt the company had disowned in writing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-and-outlook prints have moved this stock hard: +40.4% (2026-05-05), +18.0% (2025-11-05), +28.9% (2025-08-05); but the Aug 2026 raise opened ~-6% / traded -10.9% intraday before closing +1.35%, so a met-and-raised guide alone has been sold intraday.
findings.why_not_priced: The statement is public, but if the market still believed it the stock would not be 33% lower in 20 sessions and 50% off its high at ~2x lower price; the drawdown tracks the neocloud credit scare (CoreWeave/Nebius) not a DOCN data point. It lands inside the guide, so it is a met-guide expectation, sized small.
findings.independence: Same company voice as the Aug 2026 guide; corroborated by RPO pre-announcement >$800m (10x y/y) on 2026-07-07: https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260707012362/en/DigitalOcean-Expects-to-Report-Record-Q2-2026-Results-with-RPO-to-Exceed-%24800M-Up-More-Than-10X-Year-Over-Year . Shares the Sept 10 document with the financing finding.

findings.finding: DigitalOcean signed a $725m equipment finance facility with MUFG et al. (accordion to $1.025bn, which it intends to exercise; SOFR swap +2.75%, 90% of equipment cost, amortising to 2030) to buy GPUs/CPUs for 'demand expected in 2027 and 2028' -- financing that funds contracted demand (RPO >$800m, first nine-figure AI-native commitments) rather than distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior financings were sold: the Aug 2025 $500m convert fell 10.6% on the day; the July 2026 convert repurchase/registered direct also weighed. This facility is non-dilutive.
findings.why_not_priced: In the October neocloud selloff the market priced DOCN alongside CoreWeave's debt (CoreWeave 2030 bonds ~16% yield); a lease facility at SOFR+275 on low (~0.7x) net leverage is a different credit, and Q3 call will be first chance to show capacity coming online against RPO. If priced, DOCN would have decoupled from CRWV/NBIS in October; it did not.
findings.independence: Same Sept 10 document as finding 1 (8-K body vs exhibit). Corroborating use of funds: Q2 release nine-figure customer commitments https://app.sentisense.ai/stories/digitalocean-delivers-29-percent-revenue-growth-and-raises-outlook-08052026

findings.finding: Hyperscaler Q3 prints since DOCN last spoke (Oct 28-29): Azure +48% cc with demand exceeding capacity, AWS fastest growth since Q4 2021 with older GPU training instances selling short-term at a premium versus H1, Google Cloud capacity-constrained, and Azure price increases (25% on v1/v2 VMs) from Feb 2027 -- an industry-wide demand and pricing umbrella for a smaller cloud.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct record of DOCN reacting to hyperscaler prints; its +40% May 2026 move came on AI ARR acceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: DOCN fell further (-8.3% over 5 days) through the week those prints landed, so the market did not read hyperscaler capacity scarcity across to DOCN; a DOCN Q4/2027 commentary confirming spillover demand would be the transmission. Proxy, not company-confirmed; the article also notes large AI customers locked into hyperscaler backlogs could crowd out smaller providers, cutting both ways.
findings.independence: Proxy. Partial corroboration from GPU rental price series (next finding), a different source.

findings.finding: GPU rental prices kept rising into Q4: Nebius raised on-demand H100 from $3.85 to $4.50/GPU-hr effective 2026-10-01, DeepInfra hiked GPU-hour rates on 2026-10-22, and SemiAnalysis' 1-yr H100 index rose ~40% from $1.70 (Oct 2025) to $2.35 (Mar 2026) -- supportive of DOCN GPU-droplet pricing and utilisation in Q3/Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured; AI ARR (+212% to $234m in Q2) is the line DOCN has traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side preview commentary (Piper, Oct 21) focuses on valuation and 2027 growth, not on GPU unit pricing; rising rents would show up as AI ARR/NRR upside on the call. Proxy and also a cost signal (new GPUs cost more), so sized small.

findings.finding: DOCN's 33.5% 20-day fall (to $91.24, -49.7% from the $187.50 high) coincided with a sector credit scare -- CoreWeave down ~37% in October with its 2030 bonds near 16%, Nebius -25% in the week to Oct 16 with 'no negative company news' -- and DOCN had no company release in that period other than its earnings-date notice; a print that merely meets guide resets the gap between DOCN and leveraged neoclouds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Run-up into prints has preceded large up-moves before (May 2026 +40%), but the baseline's 8.3-pt put skew says the option market is paying for further downside.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had separated DOCN from CoreWeave's balance sheet the stock would not have fallen in step (10%+ on Oct 14-16, ~$128 -> $98 by Oct 16 per MarketBeat). Against an 8.3-pt put skew, so kept small: the market may instead be pricing a capex/FCF reset that DOCN shares with the sector.

findings.finding: Capex is guided to climb steeply into 2027 and FY26 adjusted FCF margin was already trimmed to 11-13%; since then Amazon cited DRAM/NAND shortages pushing its capex up and hardware inflation reaching price lists in 2027, which raises the risk DOCN's Q3 call lowers FCF/margin framing or 2027 capex efficiency even if revenue meets guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 print opened down ~6% and traded -10.9% intraday despite a revenue beat and raise, with coverage attributing the selling to capex and the FCF-margin trim; it closed +1.35%.
findings.why_not_priced: The FCF trim itself is public and partly priced; the memory-cost inflation since the hyperscaler prints (Oct 29-30) is new and DOCN has not addressed it. Put skew agrees with this sign, so much of it is likely in the price.

findings.finding: DigitalOcean ended a major promotional discount campaign in early July 2026 (stock fell ~7.9% that week), so Q3 is the first full quarter at standard rates, testing whether promotion-driven customer adds and growth hold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The promo end itself cost ~7.9% in a session (July 2026); the Aug 4 print (Q2, partly promo-affected) was beaten-then-sold intraday.
findings.why_not_priced: Management guided Q3 after the promo ended, so the guide should embed it; the risk is to customer counts/NRR commentary rather than revenue. Public since July, sized small.

findings.finding: CEO Padmanabhan Srinivasan filed Form 144s on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-21 with Form 4 sales, the CFO and CAO sold on 2026-09-01 (10b5-1, tax-withholding), and insiders made 11 open-market sales and no purchases in the six months to late August, including Access Industries' 3.3m-share ~$496m block.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction to insider filings.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly pre-arranged 10b5-1 and tax sales; no insider bought into the 50% drawdown, which would have been visible had insiders seen value. Small.

findings.finding: Piper Sandler (James Fish) upgraded DOCN to Overweight from Neutral on 2026-10-21 while cutting its target to $126 from $142, citing the near-50% pullback; it frames the Nov 3 test as the 32-34% Q3 guide and >50% 2027 growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stock rose ~2% on the upgrade day and then fell further to $91.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the wire and therefore largely priced; filed because it shows sell-side targets being cut toward spot, i.e. expectations reset lower into the print.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly positive against an 8.3-pt put skew and a -33.5% 20-day run-up; the run-up is explained by a sector credit scare rather than DOCN news, which is why the lean is kept at p_up 55 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside guide): CFO reaffirmation lands inside the company's own guide, cut 1.5 -> 0.75.
Lesson 5 (proxy): hyperscaler-read-across is macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by DOCN, cut 1.0 -> 0.75; GPU pricing proxy left at 0.5.
Lesson 7 (skew): sector-derating positioning finding signs against an 8.3-pt put skew, cut 1.0 -> 0.5.
Lesson 1/priced: FCF-trim negative was already public in August and agrees with the skew, cut -1.5 -> -1.0; promo-end negative public since July and embedded in the guide, cut -0.75 -> -0.5.
'In the wire is priced': Piper upgrade cut 0.25 -> 0.1.
Lesson 4 (financing): asked what the money buys (contracted RPO/capacity), kept the facility at +0.5 positive.
